correctness.rationale: Proof independently reconstructed: Q is symmetric idempotent with 0<Q_ee<=1 equal to effective resistance; C=I-Q gives exact column gap 2R_e-1. Max-column norm subtraction is bounded below by the smallest column gap. Dirichlet energy trial at potential 1/2 gives R_e>=4/(p+q+2)>=2/(Delta+1). Optimizing the common exterior potential gives the precise degree-pair inequality; Euler–Lagrange harmonic equations prove adjacent-true-twin iff equality when p,q>=2; bridge and K2 boundaries are handled. Explicit K_(Delta+1) transfer currents prove exact sharpness for all Delta>=1. Exact Fraction calculations passed 74 samples/635 columns but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural Banach-space structural question—under what local graph sparsity conditions is the canonical cut projection no smaller than its complementary cycle projection?—uniformly over arbitrary connected graphs. It gives a best-possible every-degree lower gap, a sharp degree-three/degree-four dominance transition, a more flexible local criterion permitting high-degree hubs, and a complete local equality characterization. Unlike a recomputation of a graph family, the theorem supplies a graph-uniform sharp phase threshold; it does not claim the elementary resistance inequalities as novel.
